fact: The Ministry of Health's HMIS unit describes itself as custodian of the digital health systems, with its own in-country developers working on CMIS and technical support from the US State Department-funded Data.FI project.
The HMIS unit reports user feedback sessions in the first quarter of 2026 with clinicians using CMIS in big hospitals in Piggs Peak and in smaller remote facilities such as Mahlangatsha Clinic.
The HMIS unit says that in the first quarter of 2026 its developers completed training with OpenFn that produced automated, FHIR-aligned data flows from CMIS's SQL Server to DHIS2.
The HMIS unit says that in the first quarter of 2026 CMIS-to-DHIS2 data reporting was strengthened with automated, FHIR-aligned data flows from SQL Server into DHIS2.

WHO Eswatini reports that DHIS2 was introduced nationally in 2024 as a single platform bringing together health data that had sat in separate programme databases, Eswatini being among the last seven countries in the African region to introduce it; in 2024 test and production servers were set up, a national Health Sector Indicator Compendium finalised, dashboards built and 25 Strategic Information Officers trained in configuration.
WHO Eswatini reports that in November 2024 it sent two consultants from its Regional Office to help the country roll out DHIS2, for which a domain and URL were already in place.

WHO Eswatini describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health's platform, rolled out by the Ministry of Health with the Ministry of ICT and WHO and with the national M&E team mentored for national ownership, while stating that in 2024 it was hosted on UNICEF servers and that limited local hosting capacity and dependence on external technical support put its sustainability and national data sovereignty at risk.

WHO Eswatini reports that in November 2024 two consultants from its Regional Office, working with the country office and the Ministry of Health's M&E team, set up DHIS2 for Eswatini, customised its reporting tools and trained the M&E team to customise data collection tools and to integrate it with the Client Management Information System and other databases.

WHO Eswatini places DHIS2 within the Ministry of Health's Strategic Health Information Department, run by its M&E unit, and says that at set-up in November 2024 its domain and URL were hosted on UNICEF servers and that the M&E unit still needed WHO technical support and IT equipment to make it fully functional.

WHO Eswatini cites the end-term review of the National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2019-2023 as finding substantial progress in automating health facility clinical systems through deployment of the Client Management Information System, with data gaps and system integration remaining a barrier; the newsletter gives no date for the finding, so its published date of December 2024 is used.

Data.FI reports that the Ministry of Health's CMIS, a centralised EMR, was in use at 75% (247 of 327) of healthcare facilities, a share of all facilities rather than of primary clinics alone, and held data on over 85% of all people on HIV treatment; the figure is for the reporting period ending March 2024.

Data.FI calls CMIS the integrated primary healthcare EMR, names King Sobhuza II Public Health Unit as a CMIS site and reports CMIS training of clinical staff at Raleigh Fitkin Memorial Hospital in Manzini region on 26 March 2024; the document does not give the facilities' tiers, so the hospital is read as T2 and primary healthcare as T4.

Data.FI describes CMIS as a centralised EMR used at the point of service, with fingerprint scanners so that a health record opens only when the person is present, and reports that the Strategic Information Department's Chief Officer mandated all facilities to use it as their primary data collection system; a Master Patient Index had been built and tested on government servers but is not reported as live.
Data.FI describes CMIS as led by the Ministry of Health, under the stewardship of the Chief Officer of its Strategic Information Department, with Data.FI supporting system development.

Data.FI, a PEPFAR-funded USAID cooperative agreement ending 14 December 2025, reports that it funds and carries out CMIS system development, security assessment and facility network support; the document states no domestic budget line.

Data.FI reports that between October 2023 and March 2024 the Strategic Information Department's Chief Officer mandated all facilities to use CMIS as their primary data collection system, CMIS dashboards reached 236 sites (97% of sites on CMIS), and a minimum viable inpatient module was deployed on a test instance.

A Ministry of Health and Data.FI poster states that CMIS keeps one record per citizen on a centralised, browser-based architecture accessible across all facilities, registers a patient by retrieving demographics from the national population registry on the national Personal Identification Number, and gives coordinated care across multiple settings; the poster is undated, so its published date of November 2023 is used.

The poster states that the Ministry of Health's HMIS Unit chose to develop CMIS as a customised solution and that the CMIS project team is made up of Ministry of Health and Data.FI experts; undated, so the published date of November 2023 is used.

The poster states that CMIS was implemented in rural and urban health facilities with support from USAID, the World Bank and the Global Fund, the Global Fund procuring the hardware and infrastructure, and that a local ISP provided 1,500 GB of pooled mobile data for the backup network; no domestic budget line is stated, and the published date of November 2023 is used.

The poster states that over two years CMIS was extended beyond HIV to non-communicable diseases, key populations, communities, vaccinations, PMTCT, stock management and prescriptions, gained a laboratory diagnostics integration and deduplication, was implemented in additional rural and urban facilities as equipment allowed, and had an MTN mobile-data APN added as backup to its microwave network, with uptime tracked from FY22 Q2 to FY23 Q3; the published date of November 2023 is used.

The Central Statistical Office's 2022 vital statistics report shows, in its registration flow charts, an HMIS officer at the hospital or maternity recording birth and death outcomes in the Ministry of Health's inpatient system, producing the Ministry's hospital birth and death statistics; HMIS supplied the report with 28,541 health-institution births and 1,354 health-institution deaths for 2022.

The Central Statistical Office's 2022 vital statistics report states that the Ministry of Health modernised its health information system by establishing the Client Management Information System, with out-patient facilities networked to the National Population Register and health facilities reading patients' PINs directly from it.
